title: The metronome ladder
summary: Build a tempo table from your slow, no-mistake speed up to the target, and write each rung in the log.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four steady clicks, standing for one rung of the tempo ladder between the slow, no-mistake speed and the piece's target tempo, climbed one small step at a time.

steps.title: The metronome ladder
steps.body:
Speed is not one leap from slow to fast. It is a ladder of small steps. Skipping a rung is how a bar that was clean at a slow tempo falls apart at a fast one.

1. Find the slowest click at which the hard bar has no mistakes: that is the bottom rung.
2. Find the piece's target tempo, from your teacher or the page: that is the top rung.
3. Write out a ladder between them, in steps of about eight to ten beats a minute.
4. Climb one rung each time the bar is clean three times in a row, and step back down if a mistake returns.

A hobby metronome usually runs from 40 to 208 beats a minute, far more range than any one piece needs. There is always room for a gentle ladder rather than a single big jump.

Write the rung you reached each sitting in the Practice log, so the climb is on paper, not just a feeling.

figure.alt: The same steady four-beat click, one rung of the ladder: climbed only once the bar is clean three times in a row, and written in the log each sitting.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: find the bottom rung, no mistakes for three clean run-throughs
Sitting 2: climb one rung, three clean run-throughs, write the number in the log
Sitting 3: climb again if clean, or hold the rung and repeat if not
Sitting 4: the whole piece at the highest clean rung, then once as if recording
An old piece played once at whatever speed feels comfortable

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the piece and the highest rung you reached this week, then play it once through at that speed, hands in the frame.
